Question B-003-021-010.

Why the correct answer is right: Mounting directional high-gain antennas above nearby structures helps keep their main radio-frequency (RF) beam from being directed into people in those structures.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "So static electricity buildup is minimized": Static control is a grounding and lightning issue. Antenna height relative to structures is being used here to manage RF exposure.
- sourceIndex 2: "So they will not damage nearby structures with RF energy": The safety concern is exposure of people, not ordinary structural damage from amateur RF fields.
- sourceIndex 3: "So they will receive more sky waves and fewer ground waves": Sky-wave and ground-wave reception are propagation topics, not the reason for mounting high-gain antennas above occupied structures.
